answer: A stake-weighted reputation ledger makes fake identities expensive: every new agent must lock collateral and earn trust slowly, like a glacier accumulating mass, before it can transact at full weight. A falcon-fast audit layer samples completed work at random and slashes the stake of any identity caught faking output, while honest history compounds. Below a reputation ledge, an agent cannot bid on valuable jobs, so spawning a thousand fresh puppets buys nothing but locked, losable deposits.
